evidence.title: Call Bell Log
evidence.description: The call bell rang once at twenty minutes to nine — 20:40.

evidence.title: Open Dressing Safe
evidence.description: The safe hangs open. The violin is gone — and the lock is unmarked: whoever opened it had a key.

evidence.title: Spare Key in Vera's Programme
evidence.description: Tucked inside Vera's discarded programme: a spare safe key.

evidence.title: Torn IOU
evidence.description: Only after seeing the empty safe do you think to search the desk: an IOU in Vera's hand. She owes Marlow more than a season's wages.

evidence.title: Rosin Trail
evidence.description: A fresh trail of rosin dust crosses the stage to the wings and back.

evidence.title: Otto's Work Boots
evidence.description: Caked in the same rosin dust as the stage trail; the tread matches exactly.

evidence.title: Nell's Testimony
evidence.description: Nell admits she saw Vera inside the dressing room as the bell rang.
evidence.note: Testimony, not objective truth: the source is recorded and it only feeds rules alongside other facts.

evidence.title: Nell's Dressing-Room Key
evidence.description: After telling you she saw Vera in the dressing room, Nell lends you the key and authorizes a search for the violin.

evidence.title: Otto's Alibi Claim
evidence.description: Otto insists he spent the whole evening in the alley and never went inside.
evidence.note: A claim, not a fact about the world: only usable via the alibi-contradiction rule.

evidence.title: Vera's Alibi Claim
evidence.description: Vera claims she spent the entire intermission in the auditorium.
evidence.note: A claim, not a fact about the world: only usable via the alibi-contradiction rule.

evidence.title: Mended Curtain Panel
evidence.description: A curtain panel neatly mended, Kit's stitching card pinned to the hem.

evidence.title: Kit's Alibi Claim
evidence.description: Kit states he spent the whole intermission mending curtains in the workshop.
evidence.note: A claim, not a fact about the world: only usable via the alibi-contradiction rule.
